meta.title: Directive (EU) 2016/1919 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 October 2016 on legal aid for suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings and for requested persons in European arrest warrant proceedings

items.heading: Article 1

nationalActs.title: Legea nr. 302/2004 privind cooperarea judiciară internațională în materie penală
nationalActs.titleEn: Law no. 302/2004 on international judicial cooperation in criminal matters

items.comment:
There is no official record of any draft project of law which at least assumes the attempt to transpose the Directive.


Still, as we will show, most provisions of the Directive have a correspondent in national law, especially after the (almost complete) transposition of Directive 2013/48/EU.

items.text: 1. This Directive lays down common minimum rules concerning the right to legal aid for:
items.comment: See general comment above.

items.text: (a)suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings; and
items.comment: See general comment above.

items.text: (b)persons who are the subject of European arrest warrant proceedings pursuant to Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA (requested persons).
items.comment: See general comment above.

items.text: 2. This Directive complements Directives 2013/48/EU and (EU) 2016/800. Nothing in this Directive shall be interpreted as limiting the rights provided for in those Directives.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: As we mentioned, the transposition of Directives 2013/48/EU is incomplete. Regarding the transposition of Directive 2016/800/EU, the draft project of law which aims at transposing this Directive is “lost” between several institutions and authorities and nothing is heard about it since mid 2019.

items.heading: Article 2

items.text: 1. This Directive applies to suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings who have a right of access to a lawyer pursuant to Directive 2013/48/EU and who are:
items.comment: The rights provided by the Directive apply in national law starting the moment the person is notified by the competent authorities that is has the status of a suspect, irrespective of any deprivation of liberty (see Article 78 and 83 CCP on the rights of the suspect and accused). All the rights are granted until the end of the trial.

items.text: (a)deprived of liberty;

provisions.textEn:
Mandatory: legal assistance of the suspect or the accused person


Legal assistance is mandatory:

a) when the suspect or the accused person (...) is detained or arrested, even in another case (...);

items.comment: If the suspect or accused is deprived of liberty, even in another case, the CCP regulates as one of the cases where legal assistance is mandatory.

items.text: (b)required to be assisted by a lawyer in accordance with Union or national law; or
items.comment:
Although there are some provisions from Directive 2013/48/EU not transposed and although the transposition of Directive 2016/800/EU is still only a draft, we consider that the cases where the EU law requires the presence of a lawyer have a correspondent in national law.

See Articles 78, 83, 108, 307, 309 CCP as well as Article 92 CCP on the rights of the lawyer of the suspect or accused.

items.text: (c)required or permitted to attend an investigative or evidence-gathering act, including as a minimum the following:
items.comment: See Article 92 CCP.

items.text: (i)identity parades;
(ii)confrontations;
(iii)reconstructions of the scene of a crime.
2. This Directive also applies, upon arrest in the executing Member State, to requested persons who have a right of access to a lawyer pursuant to Directive 2013/48/EU.

nationalActs.title: Legea nr. 302/2004 privind cooperarea judiciară internațională în materie penală
nationalActs.titleEn: Law no. 302/2004 on international judicial cooperation in criminal matters

provisions.textEn:
Detention of the requested person


(1) The measure of detention of the requested person can be taken by the prosecutor only after his / her listening in the presence of the defender

Rights of the person arrested under a European arrest warrant


(2) The arrested person has the right to be assisted by a defender chosen or appointed ex officio.

items.comment: See Articles 101 and 106 from Law no. 302/2004.

items.text: 3. This Directive also applies, under the same conditions as provided for in paragraph 1, to persons who were not initially suspects or accused persons but become suspects or accused persons in the course of questioning by the police or by another law enforcement authority.

provisions.textEn:
The rights of the accused person

 

During the criminal trial, the accused has the following rights:

c) the right to have a lawyer elected, and if he does not designate one, in the cases of compulsory assistance, the right to be appointed a lawyer ex officio;

Communication of rights and obligations

 

(1) The judicial body communicates to the suspect or the accused person the quality in which he is heard, the act provided by the criminal law for the commission of which the suspect is suspected or for which the criminal action was initiated and its legal classification.

(2) The rights stipulated in Article 83 (...)

Informing about the status of suspect

 

Before the first hearing, the person who has acquired the status of suspect is informed of this quality, the fact for which the suspect, his legal classification, the procedural rights provided in Article 83, drafting a minute in this regard.

Commencement of criminal proceedings

 

(2) The commencement of the criminal action is communicated to the defendant by the criminal prosecution body who calls him to hear him. The provisions of Article 108 are applied accordingly, a report being concluded in this regard.

The rights of the suspect


The suspect has the rights provided by law for the accused person, unless the law provides otherwise.

items.comment: See Article 78, 83, 108, 307 and 309 CCP.

items.text: 4. Without prejudice to the right to a fair trial, in respect of minor offences:

(a)where the law of a Member State provides for the imposition of a sanction by an authority other than a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters, and the imposition of such a sanction may be appealed or referred to such a court; or
items.comment:
The only case which subsume to this hypothesis in Romanian law is the waiver of prosecution solution, regulated by Article 318 CCP.

This solution can be decided by the public prosecutor in cases where the law stipulates the penalty of the fine or the punishment of imprisonment for a maximum of 7 years, and when there is no public interest in the prosecution. The solution of the prosecutor must be checked for both legality and opportunity by the preliminary chamber judge (see Article 318 para. 12 et seq., amended by Emergency Ordinance no. 18/2016, following decision no. 23/2016 of the Constitutional Court). Therefore, in front of the court (in this case the preliminary chamber judge), the general standards apply. In addition, even in the case of minor offences, since the CCP makes no distinction, starting the moment the person acquires the status of suspect all the rights enshrined by Article 78 CCP (including access to legal counsel) are applicable.

items.text: (b)where deprivation of liberty cannot be imposed as a sanction;
items.comment: The CCP makes no distinction whether deprivation of liberty cannot be imposed as a sanction at the end of the trial. Hence, since the person acquires the status of suspect, Article 78 and 83 CCP provides her all the rights, including the ones proscribed by this Directive.

items.text: this Directive applies only to the proceedings before a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters.
items.comment: The competence for imposing sanctions - even in relation to relatively minor offences - belongs only to courts with jurisdiction in criminal matters.

items.text: In any event, this Directive applies when a decision on detention is taken, and during detention, at any stage of the proceedings until the conclusion of the proceedings.
items.comment: According to the Romanian legislation, in all these case, we are in the presence of an ongoing (pending) criminal trial (even if not on the merits). Hence, all the general standars apply. Since deprivation of liberty is imposed, we are as well in the case of compulsory (mandatory) legal assistance – in these cases, if the person lacks sufficient resources to pay for the assistance of a certain lawyer, one will be appointed by the authorities free of charge (according to a protocol with the local bar).

items.text: For the purposes of this Directive, ‘legal aid’ means funding by a Member State of the assistance of a lawyer, enabling the exercise of the right of access to a lawyer.
items.heading: Article 3

provisions.textEn:
Payment of the state’s advanced expenses in case of renunciation of the criminal prosecution, conviction, postponement of the application of the punishment or renunciation of the application of the punishment



(1) In case of renunciation of the criminal prosecution, conviction, postponement of the application of the punishment or renunciation of the application of the punishment, the suspect or, as the case may be, the defendant is obliged to pay the legal expenses advanced by the state, except the expenses regarding the ex-lawyers and the designated interpreters. by the judicial bodies, which remain the responsibility of the state.

nationalActs.title: Ordonanța de Urgență nr. 51/2008 privind ajutorul public judiciar în materie civilă
nationalActs.titleEn: Emergency Ordinance no. 51/2008 regarding judicial public aid in civil matters

provisions.textEn: The judicial public assistance provided by this emergency ordinance is granted in civil, commercial, administrative, labor and social insurance cases, as well as in other cases, except for criminal cases.

items.comment: Legal aid as provided by Article 3 from the Directive is regulated by Government Emergency Ordinance no. 51/2008. The definition and the criteria correspond in general to the Directive, but, unfortunately, there is an explicit provision that the Ordinance does not apply in criminal cases. In such cases only the provisions of CCP apply.

items.heading: Article 4

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons who lack sufficient resources to pay for the assistance of a lawyer have the right to legal aid when the interests of justice so require.
items.comment: Such an obligation exists for the authorities only in cases where legal assistance is mandatory.

items.text: 2. Member States may apply a means test, a merits test, or both to determine whether legal aid is to be granted in accordance with paragraph 1.

provisions.textEn:
Mandatory legal assistance of the suspect or the accused person


Legal assistance is mandatory:

a) when the suspect or the accused is a minor, admitted to a detention center or to an educational center, when he is detained or arrested, even in another case, when against him the security measure of medical admission was ordered, even in another cause, as well as in other cases provided by law;

b) if the judicial body considers that the suspect or the defendant could not defend himself;

c) during the preliminary chamber procedure and during the trial in cases where the law stipulates for the crime committed for life imprisonment or the imprisonment of more than 5 years.

items.comment:
Such an obligation exists for the authorities only in cases where legal assistance is mandatory.

 

The cases for mandatory legal assistance are regulated explicit in the CCP. The only case in which a test can intervene, as the legal provisions is not very clear is the case where the judicial body considers that the suspect or the accused could not defend himself. In practice this usually happens if the person can not read or write, it has some mental handicap etc.

items.text: 3. Where a Member State applies a means test, it shall take into account all relevant and objective factors, such as the income, capital and family situation of the person concerned, as well as the costs of the assistance of a lawyer and the standard of living in that Member State, in order to determine whether, in accordance with the applicable criteria in that Member State, a suspect or an accused person lacks sufficient resources to pay for the assistance of a lawyer.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: There is no such concept in national legislation. Judicial help regarding legal assistance is accorded by the civil law only in other cases than criminal ones.

items.text: 4. Where a Member State applies a merits test, it shall take into account the seriousness of the criminal offence, the complexity of the case and the severity of the sanction at stake, in order to determine whether the interests of justice require legal aid to be granted. In any event, the merits test shall be deemed to have been met in the following situations:
items.comment:
As mentioned before, such criteria and procedure can be found in Government Emergency Ordinance no. 51/2008; unfortunately, this Ordinance does not apply in criminal cases.

For criminal cases, the CCP is applied, which guarantees the rights, as legal assistance is mandatory in cases envisaged below at letters a-b.

items.text: (a)where a suspect or an accused person is brought before a competent court or judge in order to decide on detention at any stage of the proceedings within the scope of this Directive; and

provisions.textEn:
Retention

(5) The detention measure may be taken only after the hearing of the suspect or the accused, in the presence of the chosen or ex officio lawyer.

Solution of the proposal of preventive arrest during the criminal investigation


(5) In all cases, the legal assistance of the defendant by a lawyer, chosen or appointed ex officio, is obligatory.

Taking the measure of home arrest by the judge of rights and freedoms


(6) The legal assistance of the accused and the participation of the prosecutor are mandatory.

items.text: (b)during detention.

provisions.textEn:
Compulsory legal assistance of the suspect or the accused



Legal assistance is mandatory:


a) when the suspect or the accused is (...) admitted to a detention center or to an educational center, when he is detained or arrested, even in another case, when against him the security measure of medical admission was ordered, even in another cause (...);

items.text: 5. Member States shall ensure that legal aid is granted without undue delay, and at the latest before questioning by the police, by another law enforcement authority or by a judicial authority, or before the investigative or evidence-gathering acts referred to in point (c) of Article 2(1) are carried out.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: Before questioning or executing investigative or evidence-gathering acts, the judicial organs inform the suspect or accused person about his rights, according to Article 83 and 78 CCP. Among these rights is the one to be assisted by a lawyer. The legal assistance is a right for the suspect or accused persons and not an obligation for the judicial organs – this is the case only when legal assistance is mandatory according to the CCP (see Article 90 a-c from the CCP, above mentioned).

items.text: 6. Legal aid shall be granted only for the purposes of the criminal proceedings in which the person concerned is suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
As mentioned before, the concept of free of charge legal aid is regulated by Government Emergency Ordinance no. 51/2008; unfortunately, this Ordinance does not apply in criminal cases.


In criminal cases, mandatory legal assistance, representing an obligation for the authorities, can be found only in cases regulated by Article 90 a-c from the CCP.

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Legal aid in European arrest warrant proceedings
items.comment:
Law. no. 236/2017 explicitly mentions amending Law no. 302/2004 in order to transpose this Directive 2013/48.

Generally, EAW proceedings involve deprivation of liberty, in order for the EAW to be executed. In all cases, presuming detention is not involved, another preventive measure will be ordered (house arrest or judicial control) – in all these cases, legal assistance is mandatory

items.text: 1. The executing Member State shall ensure that requested persons have a right to legal aid upon arrest pursuant to a European arrest warrant until they are surrendered, or until the decision not to surrender them becomes final.

nationalActs.title: Legea nr. 302/2004 privind cooperarea judiciară internațională în materie penală
nationalActs.titleEn: Law no. 302/2004 on international judicial cooperation in criminal matters

provisions.textEn:
Detention of the requested person


(1) The measure of detention of the requested person can be taken by the prosecutor only after his / her listening in the presence of the defender

The rights of the person arrested under a European arrest warrant


(2) The arrested person has the right to be assisted by a defender chosen or appointed ex officio.

items.comment:
Law. no. 236/2017 explicitly mentioned amending Law no. 302/2004 in order to transpose this Directive 2013/48, inter alia, regarding the legal assistance of an attorney.



Upon arrest pursuant to a European arrest warrant, legal assistance is always mandatory.

items.text: 2. The issuing Member State shall ensure that requested persons who are the subject of European arrest warrant proceedings for the purpose of conducting a criminal prosecution and who exercise their right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State to assist the lawyer in the executing Member State in accordance with Article 10(4) and (5) of Directive 2013/48/EU have the right to legal aid in the issuing Member State for the purpose of such proceedings in the executing Member State, in so far as legal aid is necessary to ensure effective access to justice.

nationalActs.title: Legea nr. 302/2004 privind cooperarea judiciară internațională în materie penală
nationalActs.titleEn: Law no. 302/2004 on international judicial cooperation in criminal matters

provisions.textEn:
Rights of the person arrested under a European arrest warrant



(3) The prosecutor or, as the case may be, the executing court notifies the detained or arrested person that he has the right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State of the European arrest warrant and to communicate with him, directly or through through the lawyer elected or appointed ex officio in Romania, under the conditions provided by the Romanian law and with the assurance of confidentiality.


(4) If the detained or arrested person shows that he understands to exercise this right, the prosecutor or the executing court shall inform the issuing authority of the European arrest warrant without delay. The information transmitted by the issuing authority, by any means which leaves a written trace, shall be communicated without delay to the requested person through the administration of the place of detention.

Additional information and warranties


(3) If the requested person, who is under arrest in the executing state, exercises his right to appoint a lawyer in Romania, the Romanian court issuing the European arrest warrant shall transmit, upon request and without undue delay, to the executing authority the information regarding the panel of lawyers entitled to practice in one of the member bars of the National Union of Bars in Romania. The information may also be transmitted electronically.


(4) The role of the Romanian lawyer, designated according to par. (3), is to provide assistance to the lawyer in the executing Member State, by providing him with information and advice, in order to allow the requested person to formulate his defenses in the procedure of executing the European arrest warrant.

Legal assistance is mandatory:

 

a) when the suspect or the accused is (..) arrested, even in another case (...);

items.comment:
Law. no. 236/2017 explicitly mentions amending Law no. 302/2004 in order to transpose this Directive 2013/48, inter alia, the provisions of Article 10 para. 4 and 5 of Directive 2013/48/EU.

For this, see Article 91 para. 3 and 4 from Law no. 302/2004.


If Romanian is the issuing Member State, the requirements of the Directive are in all cases respected, if the person is arrested or in any way deprived of liberty in the executing Member State (either during the European arrest warrant proceedings or in another case). The reason for this is based on the wording of Article 90 a final thesis CCP, where mandatory legal assistance is provided in the case where the suspect or accused person is arrested, even in another case.


In case the person is not arrested in the executing Member State, although the provisions of Article 91 para. 3 and 4 from Law no. 302/2004 impose on the Romanian authorities to transmit information about lawyers from National Bar, there is no distinct obligation to grant legal aid.

items.text: 3. The right to legal aid referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 may be subject to a means test in accordance with Article 4(3), which shall apply mutatis mutandis.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
As mentioned before there is no such concept in national legislation. Judicial help regarding legal assistance is accorded by the civil law only in other cases than criminal ones.

In addition, we already showed that in case of para. 1 legal assistance is mandatory, while in most cases from para. 2 the solution will be the same.

items.heading: Article 6
items.subHeading: Decisions regarding the granting of legal aid

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
As mentioned before, no specific legal instrument has been enacted with a view to implement the Directive. There is no information about at least a draft proposal on the topic.

Therefore, there is no concept of legal aid in criminal matters.

items.text: 1. Decisions on whether or not to grant legal aid and on the assignment of lawyers shall be made, without undue delay, by a competent authority. Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that the competent authority takes its decisions diligently, respecting the rights of the defence.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: Since there is no legal aid in criminal matters regulated, there is no possibility to decide on whether or not to grant legal. In criminal matters legal assistance is either mandatory, where the authorities will appoint an ex officio lawyer or the presence of an attorney is optional (even where the requirements of the Directive regarding legal aid would be fulfilled).

items.text: 2. Member States shall take necessary measures to ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons are informed in writing if their request for legal aid is refused in full or in part.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: Since there is no legal aid in criminal matters regulated, there is no provision about informing suspects and accused persons if their request for legal aid is refused in full or in part.

items.heading: Article 7
items.subHeading: Quality of legal aid services and training

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: Since the Directive was not transposed, the national legislation lacks specific provisions dealing with these aspects. Some correspondence can be inferred with other provision, regulating the general duties of the lawyer (according to Law no. 51/1995).

items.text: 1. Member States shall take necessary measures, including with regard to funding, to ensure that:

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: (a)there is an effective legal aid system that is of an adequate quality; and

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: As there is no legal aid system in criminal matters, reference can be made only to the system envisaged by Ordinance no. 51/2008 in civil matters. Still, we already showed that at current time this Ordinance is precluded from application in criminal cases.

items.text: (b)legal aid services are of a quality adequate to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, with due respect for the independence of the legal profession.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
We can mention here only the general duty of the lawyers, as provided by Article 39 from Law no. 51/1995.


According to Article 39 (Duties of lawyers):


(1) The lawyer is obliged to study thoroughly the cases that have been entrusted to him, employed or ex officio, to present at each term to the courts or to the criminal investigation bodies or to other institutions, according to the entrusted mandate, to show conscientiousness and professional probity, to plead with dignity against the judges and the parties in the process, to submit written conclusions or hearing notes whenever the nature or the difficulty of the case requires it or the court has to this effect. Failure to comply with these professional duties constitutes a disciplinary offense.


(2) The lawyer is obliged to do all the diligence to defend the rights, freedoms and legitimate interests of the clients and to use the means provided by law, which he

considers favorable to them.


(3) The lawyer is obliged to refrain from assisting and advising a client in the accomplishment by him of acts or facts that could constitute crimes.


(4) The lawyer is entitled to withdraw immediately and to renounce the assistance and representation of the client if his actions and goals, apparently legal at the beginning of the assistance and / or representation, prove, during the course, as criminal.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that adequate training is provided to staff involved in the decision-making on legal aid in criminal proceedings and in European arrest warrant proceedings.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: No such provision exists in national legislation.

items.text: 3. With due respect for the independence of the legal profession and for the role of those responsible for the training of lawyers, Member States shall take appropriate measures to promote the provision of adequate training to lawyers providing legal aid services.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
We can mention here only the general duty of the lawyers to attend various forms of continuous professional training under the auspices of the National Institute for the Training and Improvement of the Lawyers

 

See Article 22 from Law no 51/1995:

(2) The trainee lawyers, after registering in the bar, have the obligation to attend the courses of the National Institute for the Training and Improvement of the Lawyers, during the internship period.

 

(4) The definitive lawyer is obliged to attend the forms of continuous professional training organized by the bar, the National Institute for the Training and Improvement of Lawyers or by the forms of practicing the profession, under the conditions provided by the Statute of the lawyer profession.

items.text: 4. Member States shall take the necessary measures to ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons have the right, upon their request, to have the lawyer providing legal aid services assigned to them replaced, where the specific circumstances so justify.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: In criminal matters the replacement of the ex officio lawyer (in cases of mandatory legal assistance) is possible, on a case by case basis, e.g., if the lawyer fails to fulfill his duties, if there is a conflict between the client and the lawyer, etc. Although such cases are not explicitly provided by the legislation, the replacement operates at the request of either the person or the lawyer, as part of the right to an effective defence (since otherwise is hard to consider such a defence would be accomplished).

items.text: Member States shall ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons have an effective remedy under national law in the event of a breach of their rights under this Directive.
items.heading: Article 8

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: Having in mind the lack of transposition, at current time explicit effective remedies refer only to case where the provisions on mandatory legal assistance are not respected. In this case, an absolute nullity case is present.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that the particular needs of vulnerable suspects, accused persons and requested persons are taken into account in the implementation of this Directive.
items.heading: Article 9

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: Due to the lack of tranposition, there is no such provision in national law.
